heading: Start with a question
intro: One-click templates: a common question, a short answer, and a fully-configured simulation that demonstrates it. No jargon required.

agent-slow-turn5.question: Why is my agent slow after turn 5?
agent-slow-turn5.tagline: Un-cached agent loops re-prefill the whole conversation every turn
agent-slow-turn5.blurb: Every turn an agent appends tool output and its own reply to the transcript. Without prefix caching, the server re-prefills the ENTIRE conversation on every turn, so turn cost grows linearly with turn count — turn 8 re-ingests everything turns 1-7 produced. This demo runs an 8-turn loop with caching OFF so you can watch per-turn prefill bars stack up; toggle "prefix caching" in the controls and the later turns collapse to just the new tokens.

prefix-caching-128k.question: Does prefix caching help at 128K context?
prefix-caching-128k.tagline: Yes — and the bigger the shared prefix, the bigger the win
prefix-caching-128k.blurb: Prefix caching skips re-prefilling tokens the server has already ingested for an identical prompt prefix. The win scales with the SHARED portion, not the total: at a 64K-token shared system + document prefix, every turn saves a 64K-token prefill — roughly 17 s of TTFT on an RTX 4090 (65,536 ÷ 3,800 tok/s) — and pays only for the fresh tool output. Run the demo and compare turn 1 (full prefill) with turn 2+ (delta only).

rpi5-7b.question: Can a Raspberry Pi 5 run a 7B?
rpi5-7b.tagline: It can run it — slowly, because decode is bandwidth-bound
rpi5-7b.blurb: A Pi 5 has no GPU; a 4-bit 7B fits in its 8 GB RAM but every decoded token must stream all ~4 GB of weights from LPDDR4X at ~17 GB/s. That caps decode around 8 tok/s no matter how good the software is — decode is memory-bandwidth-bound, and the Pi has very little. Prefill is even worse (~120 tok/s). The sim shows the honest numbers: first token in ~17 s, then a token every ~125 ms.

fp16-vs-int4-kv.question: FP16 vs INT4 KV cache VRAM
fp16-vs-int4-kv.tagline: Halving KV bytes doubles the context that fits — weights too
fp16-vs-int4-kv.blurb: KV cache size is bytes-per-token × context × batch, and the bytes-per-token scales directly with KV precision. For a 70B model at 128K context, FP16 KV needs ~40 GB while INT4 KV needs ~10 GB — the difference between "needs an H100" and "fits on two 24 GB cards". The catch: INT4 KV quantization is lossy for long-range attention recall. Load the demo, then flip the precision toggle to INT4 and watch the memory bar shrink 4×.
